text:
Alex Chen: quick check-in — i opened the tenant-fencing refactor RFC last week. planning to push authorization and tenant-scoping earlier in the console query pipeline so we don't scan panel rows for out-of-scope tenants. thoughts on correctness vs perf tradeoffs?
Mira Patel: moving it to the router layer would cut downstream work a lot. main downsides: we need a very low-latency tenant lookup and a clear cache invalidation strategy.
Sam Ortiz: agree on perf wins. but cache coherence across regions is tricky — if tenant metadata changes (role updates), stale fences could leak results. how do we handle eventual consistency?
Priya Nair: propose: 1) tenant fence check at ingress (router) + a small per-tenant bitset in memory to short-circuit. 2) authoritative store is PG with changefeed -> invalidate by tenant id. 3) short TTL local caches (5s) to avoid thundering.
Alex Chen: example config prototype i'm testing:
```yaml
fencing:
  mode: router
  local_ttl_seconds: 5
  changefeed_topic: console.tenant.meta.v1
  fallback_behavior: deny_on_miss
```
Mira Patel: what about audit logs for RBAC decisions? we need to keep the old downstream checks during migration to double-check and emit audit events for a month.
Sam Ortiz: also consider a soft-fail mode where router fence returns a 429-like retry hint so client can backoff and hit fallback path. avoids silent denys while we cutover.
Priya Nair: rollout plan i suggest:
- feature flag behind tenant.fencing.v2
- canary 5% requests for non-critical orgs (low usage)
- metric set: per-tenant miss rate, authz-deny-rate, avg-query-latency pre/post
- keep downstream checks enabled in shadow and compare outputs for 2 weeks
- gradual ramp 5 -> 25 -> 100
Sam Ortiz: define SLOs we can measure during canary: 99th token latency delta <= 12ms, authz false-positive rate < 0.01%. if we hit threshold, auto rollback.
Alex Chen: good call. also need a DB migration: add tenant_fence_version on panels table so old queries opt out until we flip. this helps rollback.
Mira Patel: ops notes: changefeed consumer must be idempotent and support replay from timestamp. instrument partition lag metrics.
Priya Nair: i'll draft the rollout runbook with exact queries and the `compare_shadow` script to diff results.
deploy-bot: scheduled deploy window: 2026-06-15 02:00 UTC -> will run canary rollout job if feature flag enabled.
Sam Ortiz: one more tradeoff — prefix caching: if a tenant has many panels, prefix caching in router reduces lookups but increases memory. suggest LRU with tenant-size cap.
Alex Chen: agreed. I'll prototype LRU cap and push perf numbers next week. thanks all :thumbsup:
